title: Intern Frontend Engineer
description:
Team Summary
We are a small frontend team building a web platform for ML data annotation. Our frontend work is an active balance of greenfield feature development and the continuous evolution of our established data-annotation tools. Whether architecting a new visual editor from scratch or modernizing an existing codebase, we hold all work to the same standard: architecture docs as the source of truth, small reviewed PRs, strict linting/type checks a dedicated component book for every UI element, and an AI-assisted workflow.
Job Summary
We are looking for an intern with solid TypeScript fundamentals who is eager to learn Svelte and modern frontend conventions. In this role you'll start with well-scoped tasks: UI components, component book entries, tests, small bug fixes in legacy projects under a mentor's review, and grow toward owning small features end to end. You will work with a modern stack (Svelte 5, TypeScript, Tailwind, Bun), practice AI-assisted development as a standard workflow, and ship to production behind strict quality gates in a team small enough for your work to make an immediate impact.
Responsibilities and Duties

• Implement small UI components and pages in Svelte 5 / TypeScript following the design system

• Add component book entries and write unit/browser tests for new and existing components

• Fix well-scoped bugs in the new platform and in legacy projects

• Integrate simple REST endpoints under guidance

• Participate in code review (receive feedback, and gradually review others' PRs)

• Keep type checks, lint and tests green on your changes

• Improve documentation and conventions where you find gaps

• Learn and apply AI-assisted development responsibly

Qualifications and Skills

• At least 1 year of experience and/or a GitHub profile with pet projects available for the team review

• Solid TypeScript fundamentals

• HTML/CSS knowledge

• Familiarity with at least one modern frontend framework (any - Svelte, React, Vue)

• Good understanding of client-server communication

• Git basics

• Ability to understand technical documentation and follow engineering guidelines

• Good written and spoken English (preferably B1+)

Nice to have

• Solid knowledge of Svelte/SvelteKit and Tailwind

• Experience with unit testing (Vitest/Jest)

• Hands-on experience with AI-assisted workflows

We offer multiple benefits that include

• The environment of equal opportunities, transparent and value-based corporate culture, and an individual approach to each team member

• Competitive compensation and perks

• Gig-contract (6 months)

• 21 paid vacation days per year, paid public holidays according to Ukrainian legislation

• Medical insurance is provided from day one. Sick leaves and medical leaves are available

• Remote working mode is available within Ukraine only

• Free meals, fruits, and snacks when working in the office.

Our Summer Internship Program is designed for students entering their final year of university who are eager to gain meaningful, real-world experience in a fast paced, collaborative, and professional environment.

As a Summer Intern, you'll participate in a comprehensive onboarding experience led by our University Relations team to set you up for success from day one. title: Lead Recruiter | Executive
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp is hiring a Lead Recruiter to own Director-level and above hiring across our G&A and business functions. You will lead some of the company’s most critical leadership searches, partnering directly with senior stakeholders to identify and hire leaders who will shape Ramp’s next stage of growth.

You will own searches from initial scoping through close, partnering directly with executives and senior leaders across the business. You will be expected to develop real fluency in each area you support, translate ambiguous business needs into clear hiring strategies, and bring an independent point of view on talent.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally strong at research, assessment, stakeholder partnership, and closing. You should be comfortable challenging assumptions, navigating sensitive and confidential searches, and creating structure without slowing the business down. You should be a self-starter who thrives in ambiguity, builds pipelines from scratch, and takes ownership of moving searches forward even when the role, target profile, or process is still taking shape.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own full-cycle recruiting for Director-level and above roles across G&A and business functions, from intake and market mapping through offer and close.

- Develop real fluency in the functions you support and quickly build context when taking on a new area, so you can identify the signals that distinguish exceptional leaders beyond title, company, and tenure.

- Build proactive pipelines through market research, targeted sourcing, referrals, and thoughtful engagement with passive candidates. Independently build momentum on confidential searches where broad outreach or an existing pipeline may not be available.

- Develop assessment approaches that surface a candidate’s leadership effectiveness, functional expertise, and ability to operate at Ramp’s pace and scale.

- Move fluidly across functions, evolving role definitions, and competing priorities while maintaining a consistently high bar for talent, execution, and candidate experience.

- Exercise discretion throughout sensitive searches, managing candidate information and stakeholder communication with sound judgment.

 

WHAT YOU NEED

- 6+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience.

- A track record of independently leading complex senior-level searches from initial scoping through accepted offer.

- Ability to advise senior leaders, challenge requirements, and influence hiring decisions through clear communication, market insight, and data.

- Demonstrated ability to build fluency in unfamiliar functions, context-switch across very different searches, and maintain strong judgment as priorities and scope change.

- A high level of ownership and comfort with ambiguity. You can turn an open-ended business need into an actionable search, build a pipeline from scratch, and drive progress without waiting for direction.

- Strong closing skills, including experience navigating competing offers, senior candidates, and sensitive searches.

We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Full Time Clinician (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

​
A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“I love seeing health plan members at home. You get a better picture of their health when you see where they live.” - Erica R., PA

• Keep projects moving. Turn agreed deliverables into clear tasks, owners, due dates, dependencies, and next steps. Follow up on stalled handoffs and flag blockers early.

What You'll Bring

Experience That's Helpful

What Success Looks Like

If you love bringing people, ideas, and details together to turn good work into something great, we'd love to hear from you. At Ami Arroyo, Inc. , every detail is an opportunity to build trust, and we're excited to meet someone who brings creativity, care, and follow-through to the process.

• Atuar diretamente com análise crítica, validação e recomendação de regramentos em motores de fraude para produtos de meios de pagamento/cartões, orientando decisões embasadas em massa de dados.

• Definir e implementar estratégias de prevenção de fraudes no onboarding de clientes e em transações financeiras, equilibrando prioridades entre as duas frentes.

• Realizar exploração de dados (SQL, Databricks) para embasar teses e desenhar soluções pragmáticas para os problemas levantados.

• Definir e ser responsável pelos KPIs estratégicos de fraude (taxa de fraude confirmada, chargeback, perda evitada), reportando performance e riscos para a Diretoria e Comitê de Risco.

• Garantir excelente comunicação e articulação com os times de Produtos e Negócios para alinhar impactos de regras e comunicar tradeoffs de decisões de fraude de maneira transparente e colaborativa.

• Avaliar novas tecnologias e fornecedores de soluções antifraude, conduzindo provas de conceito (PoC) e implementações de novas soluções e metodologias.

• Ensino superior completo em Administração, Engenharias, Matemática, Direito, Contábeis ou correlacionadas.

• Experiência comprovada em liderança de equipes (gestão de pessoas) em prevenção a fraudes, com atuação estratégica em análise de dados e implementação de processos antifraude.

• Experiência em instituições financeiras, fintechs ou mercado de pagamentos, com ownership de indicadores de perda financeira e redução de chargeback).

• Habilidade em storytelling com dados, traduzindo dados em insights claros e acionáveis.

• Domínio prático de SQL e Databricks (ou similar) para exploração de dados, diagnóstico de cenários, elaboração de relatórios e dashboards e fundamentação de hipóteses.

• Perfil analítico, pragmático e hands-on, com foco em equilibrar mitigação de riscos, perdas financeiras e boa experiência para o cliente.

The Role
 
As a Software Engineer Intern on Sovereign AI Infrastructure, you will help build the systems that make AI agents useful, reliable, and governable in high-stakes operational environments.

This is not a research-only internship. You’ll own a project with hands-on mentorship from experienced engineers, contributing to the systems that make production AI useful and trustworthy. title: People & Performance Program Manager (Remote - Mexico)
description:
About Kasa

Kasa is the leading tech-enabled hotel and apartment hotel brand and manager. We partner with owners of multifamily and boutique hospitality properties to deliver stylish, professionally managed accommodations to business and leisure travelers alike. We took the best that hotels and short-term rentals had to offer and created a new class of hospitality that is well-priced, reliable, and offers a large selection of great locations.

Unlike traditional hotel operators, we prioritize automation, AI-driven pricing, and data-driven decision-making to optimize revenue and improve guest experiences. Behind the scenes, we build technology that combines with our innovative operations to grow a globally scalable offering that delivers high-quality stays to guests. Our guests enjoy seamless check-ins, caring service, and attractive amenities - and if anything comes up, our on-site and remote guest experience team is available throughout their stay, ensuring our hospitality is rarely seen but always felt.

Role Overview

Kasa is seeking a People Program Manager to own a defined and evolving slate of People programs, including but not limited to performance scorecards, manager training and enablement, career tracks, the annual performance cycle, and engagement measurement. This role translates strategic organizational priorities into practical, well-run programs.

This role sits within Kasa’s People team and reports to the Director of People & Performance. It’s an individual contributor, program-ownership role: hands-on, analytically strong, and comfortable building repeatable systems end to end. This People Program Manager will work closely with our Senior People Business Partner, and the two roles are intended to work in close partnership with clear swim lanes. The priorities of this role are to:

• Build programs that run without being chased. Own the systems behind how we evaluate, develop, and grow people, and use AI and automation to keep them repeatable and scalable.

• Equip managers to lead well. Give our people managers the tools and training to coach their teams, give useful feedback, and grow talent.

• Give leaders a clear view of team health. Turn People data into insights and recommendations that help us spot trends and retention risks early and act on them.

Key Responsibilities & Deliverables

Performance Scorecards & Manager Enablement

• Build performance scorecards that give managers ongoing visibility into team health and impact

• Design and run manager training and enablement programs that help managers set clear expectations, coach their teams, and grow as leaders

• Build manager capability through training, resources, and job aids on the performance process

Career Tracks

• Own the career tracks framework end-to-end, including leveling, competencies, and progression criteria across functions

• Partner with functional leaders to define what good looks like at each level and keep tracks current as roles and the org evolve

• Make progression transparent for employees through clear criteria, examples, and self-assessment tools so people know what's next and how to get there

• Connect career tracks to performance, promotion, and compensation decisions so leveling stays consistent and defensible

Performance Review Cycle

• Own the annual performance cycle end-to-end, including timeline, communications, calibration, and tooling

• In partnership with key members of the People team, design the review process itself, including rating scales, self and peer input, and how performance connects to promotion and compensation decisions

• Equip managers and employees with clear guidance, resources, and job aids so the process feels useful rather than administrative

• Measure how the cycle lands through completion rates, quality of feedback, and manager and employee sentiment, then improve it each year

Engagement Measurement

• Own our engagement measurement approach, including the engagement dashbo

title: Research and Development Engineer in Artificial Intelligence - 12 months contract
description:
Who we are ?
Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools.
The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment.

Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing potential attacks, understanding the strategies available to attackers and defenders, and verifying that critical security properties are preserved. Formal verification provides rigorous methods for addressing these challenges, allowing engineers to reason about system behaviours and establish mathematical guarantees. However, applying these techniques to realistic systems remains challenging. Verification problems can involve large state spaces and complex strategic interactions, while constructing formal models and specifying security properties often requires specialised expertise.
The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges by combining formal verification with artificial intelligence. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for analysing cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. The project also investigates how AI can improve the efficiency and accessibility of these verification processes.
A central objective of VITAMIN-C is to integrate AI techniques into the verification workflow. On the computational side, AI models will be investigated to guide the exploration of large state spaces and prioritise promising verification strategies. By learning from previously verified models and their associated results, these components can help identify relevant search directions and reduce the computational effort required by verification algorithms. On the usability side, the project explores AI-assisted interfaces that support engineers in constructing formal models and specifying security properties. These interfaces may exploit natural-language processing and large language models to interpret engineering descriptions, suggest formal representations, and assist users throughout the verification process. In both cases, the correctness of verification results remains the responsibility of the underlying formal methods, which validate the outcomes produced or suggested by AI components.
Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of AI techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on developing AI components for verification guidance, investigating natural-language and LLM-based assistance for formal modelling, and integrating these capabilities into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in the preparation of training and evaluation datasets, the development of experimental benchmarks, and the assessment of the proposed approaches in terms of effectiveness, computational efficiency, and reliability. The overall objective is to make formal verification more scalable and accessible while preserving the rigorous guarantees provided by the verification framework.

Your main responsibilities will include :

• Carry out R&D work in artificial intelligence for formal verification

• Contribute to the research profile of Télécom Paris and Institut Mines-Télécom

The Role

Every customer runs on a different stack, so this role calls for real engineering depth, and you don't need a long AI resume to have it. What You'll Do

• Sit with customers' frontline staff to learn how the work actually gets done, capture the rules and exceptions that live in people's heads, and translate them into explicit logic

• Build trust with the people whose work you're automating, and treat them as the experts on their process

• Assess technical feasibility and identify which tasks are good candidates for an agent and where human review should stay in the loop

• Translate customer needs into solution designs, effort estimates, and clear scope

• Build proofs of concept and demos that show customers what an agent can do with their own workflows

• Provide build and run cost estimates (model usage, infrastructure, maintenance) to support pricing

title: Research Scientist, Soft Matter Simulations
locationText: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Your role will involve applying soft matter physics and molecular simulation expertise to accelerate the discovery, optimization, and understanding of complex soft matter systems. You will use coarse-grained and atomistic modeling, mesoscale simulation, analytical theory, and agentic AI systems to investigate polymers, colloids, surfactants, gels, liquid crystals, and formulated fluid systems with direct relevance to commercial applications.

You will work at the intersection of physics-based simulation, AI/ML, and autonomous scientific workflows. The focus is on using computational insight to identify promising formulations and material compositions, explain structure-property relationships, guide optimization campaigns, and help agents reason over simulation and experimental data in scientifically grounded ways. Desired simulation expertise covers atomistic and coarse-grained molecular dynamics, mesoscale approaches such as dissipative particle dynamics, Monte Carlo sampling, and analytical theory including self-consistent field theory, field theoretic simulation, and liquid state theory.

This is a hands-on research role for someone who can connect deep soft matter and molecular simulation expertise with software development and practical scientific impact. You will collaborate with computational scientists, AI researchers, software engineers, and experimental teams to turn simulations, models, and scientific reasoning into robust software, agentic frameworks, and closed-loop scientific workflows.

What You'll Be Building

• Implement, extend, and deploy atomistic, coarse-grained, and mesoscale simulation capabilities for soft matter systems, including MD, DPD, SCFT, Monte Carlo, and liquid state theory

• Engineer simulation software with modern scientific libraries, emphasizing testing, modularity, and reproducibility at scale on HPC and cloud infrastructure

• Translate simulation outputs into descriptors and datasets for ML models, and build predictive models to guide formulation selection and optimization

• Develop and deploy agentic AI systems that leverage simulation capabilities for autonomous scientific discovery and closed-loop experimentation

• Communicate physical insights, model limitations, and recommendations to computational, ML, and experimental collaborators

What You'll Need to Succeed

• PhD in chemical engineering, physics, materials science, chemistry, or a related field (or master's with equivalent experience)

• Strong background in soft matter physics covering polymers, colloids, surfactants, gels, or liquid crystals, with hands-on expertise in atomistic and coarse-grained MD

• Working knowledge of at least two of: DPD or other mesoscale methods, Monte Carlo, SCFT, field theoretic simulation, or liquid state theory

• Strong Python scientific software development skills; fluency with modern practices including version control, testing, code review, and packaging

• Experience running and automating simulations at scale on HPC or cloud, and integrating computational predictions into experimental or closed-loop optimization workflows

• Good familiarity with agentic AI systems, autonomous scientific workflows, or simulation-aware agents

Bonus Points For

• Experience with a compiled language (C++, Rust, or Fortran) for performance-critical simulation code, or GPU acceleration via JAX or PyTorch

• Contributions to open source simulation packages such as LAMMPS, HOOMD-blue, GROMACS, or OpenMM

• Experience developing ML potentials or applying AI/ML to soft matter simulation data and molecular property prediction

• Experience building agents that reason over or orchestrate simulation workflows, or coupling simulation to active learning and Bayesian optimization pipelines

• Publication record in soft matter theory and simulation

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Search Features & APIs (SABR)
description:
ABOUT US

Launched in 2019, Constructor is an AI-first e-commerce search and discovery platform that helps shoppers find the right products at the right time and enables leading global e-commerce brands to drive meaningful revenue and conversion gains.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The SABR team owns the top layer of request processing for product discovery. We own the service that first receives product discovery requests (autocomplete, search, browse & recommendations) & executes the entire business logic that drives product discovery. That service also functions as a gateway to parse incoming user requests, orchestrate calls across the internal services that do the ranking and retrieval, interpret their responses, and assemble the final response the customer sees. We also own the public configuration APIs customers use to control how discovery behaves, and the MCP layer that exposes all of it to AI agents.

Our team owns both platform & product components: Because of the positioning of our services, we take part in every architectural decision of our core product offering. At the same time, our goals are heavily influenced by direct customer feedback, because all product discovery-related features are either implemented in or integrated with our services.

All of our services are public APIs, so interface design and backward compatibility are a constant part of the job. But most of our attention goes to keeping them fast and up: we serve up to 15k RPS, fan out to many internal services on every request, and are expected to stay available and degrade gracefully when any of them fails or slows down.

The work is distributed systems in practice rather than in theory: request orchestration, failure isolation, caching, latency budgets, capacity planning, and the observability to know what is actually happening in production. The team is small enough that engineers own problems end to end, from design through on-call.

ABOUT YOU

You're a senior engineer who wants to own features end to end, not just close tickets. You've built and run production Python services, ideally high-traffic or latency-sensitive ones, and you've been on-call for them. You think in trade-offs: latency versus cost, a quick fix versus a durable one, a new parameter versus a public API customers can't afford to see break. You can take a feature from a rough problem statement to a design, ship it, and then make sure it behaves in production. You're comfortable leading a project with one or two other engineers and helping teammates grow along the way. When a problem is only partly defined, you ask the right questions to pin it down. When you meet an unfamiliar protocol or system, you read the spec and work out how it fits. You change your mind when someone has a better argument, and you still care about your code long after it merges.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Own the design and delivery of features and components in our services.

- Design and evolve public API endpoints with backward compatibility in mind, and contribute to architecture discussions for our services.

description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.

The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.

Operating Principles:

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.

AI-FIRST BY DEFAULT

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

- Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

- Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

- Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

- Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Deepgram is looking for a Staff Software Engineer to be the technical lead of the Console team.

Deepgram is the leader in developer-friendly building blocks for language AI: real-time transcription, voice agents, and audio intelligence at scale. The Console team owns the product surfaces that help developers discover, test, and adopt Deepgram. That includes customer-facing experiences like Console and Playground, account management (authorization, billing, analytics), agentic tooling integrations like MCP servers and SDK experiences, and internal tools that support teams across the company. These surfaces shape a customer's first impression of Deepgram and directly influence buying decisions.

In the current wave of AI-native development, developer experience is the product. The best infrastructure wins by being the easiest to trust.

 

As a Staff engineer, you'll set the technical direction for our self-serve platform and lead large, high-priority, cross-functional projects that shape the company's product-led growth. You'll partner with senior leaders in Engineering, Product, Design, Sales, and Marketing, help set priorities, and anticipate the problems we'll face before they arrive. You'll still write a lot of code. We're looking for a strong full-stack generalist with broad product instincts.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

title: Staff Software Engineer - Compiler & Spark Runtime
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset - who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Staff Software Engineer - Compiler & Spark Runtime

Location: Bellevue, WA or Menlo Park, CA

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Spark Runtime Engineering Team brings Snowflake’s performance, efficiency, and reliability to Spark workloads. Our mission is to help customers scale data processing while preserving the familiar Spark APIs and semantics they rely on. We build the compiler and runtime integration that translate Spark workloads into efficient execution on Snowflake’s cloud-native query engine. This includes tackling complex challenges in compiler infrastructure, query-plan lowering, Spark compatibility, execution integration, and end-to-end observability to deliver faster, more cost-efficient data processing at scale.

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on engineer who combines deep technical expertise with the ability to lead complex engineering initiatives and influence technical direction. You will design and build critical compiler and runtime capabilities, guide architectural decisions, and mentor engineers through technical collaboration.

ROLE OVERVIEW

You will own complex projects from design through implementation and production rollout, contribute directly to the codebase, review critical designs and code, and investigate challenging correctness, performance, and reliability issues. You will provide technical leadership for engineers building production compiler and runtime capabilities for Spark workloads on Snowflake.

In partnership with compiler, query engine, runtime, and product teams, you will translate customer needs into focused technical priorities and measurable engineering outcomes. You will lead through technical judgment, hands-on execution, mentorship, and influence-not through formal reporting relationships.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Lead the technical design and implementation of Spark query compilation and runtime integration, including intermediate representations, type resolution, semantic compatibility, query-plan transformations, and efficient SQL generation.

- Own complex engineering initiatives from problem definition and architecture through implementation, validation, and production rollout.

- Provide technical leadership to project teams by clarifying engineering trade-offs, aligning contributors, reviewing designs and code, and resolving technical blockers.

- Improve end-to-end workload performance and cost-efficiency through profiling, compilation-latency reduction, metadata-access improvements, and collaboration with query-engine teams.

- Establish strong correctness and compatibility practices, including differential testing against Apache Spark, regression coverage, and clear handling of unsupported behavior.

- Drive production quality for owned components, including observability, incident investigation, fault recovery, and safe rollout practices.

- Mentor engineers through design discussions, code reviews, debugging, and knowledge sharing, strengthening the team’s technical capabilities.

- Partner with senior technical leaders and Product Management to prioritize investments, identify dependencies, and scope deliverable engineering milestones.

- Validate changes against representative customer workloads and track measurable improvements in compatibility, latency, reliability, and cost-effic
